questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly the weather and the travel opportunities to many far away places that you rarely or never would visit

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't receive any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy through
flatmates.com.au
. I did however end up in a very weird apartment which meant I had to move in with other Danes on exchange in Brisbane. I recommend reaching out to other student going on exchange and find accommodation with them. KU didn't put me in touch with anyone going to Brisbane which meant I knew none when leaving Denmark. I regret not reaching out to students from CBS og DTU before going as accommodation would have been cheaper and more enjoyable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Australia is expensive but Brisbane is still a little cheaper than Copenhagen. I generally found it cheaper going out to eat compared to Copenhagen, while groceries were more expensive. And alcohol is expensive :((

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of student accommodation in Brisbane but it is either expensive or very bad. I recommend finding accommodation on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy. I applied for all the pre-approved courses and got in easy. Griffith's system is very stress-free

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a 24 hour student desk. I didn't use it but I know a few who got a lot of help from them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Griffith has a lot of campuses. I recommend determining whether you want to stay in Brisbane or Gold Coast beforehand. I went to Nathan (Brisbane South), which is the main campus in Brisbane but it is not in the city. The campuses that Griffith has in the city of Brisbane are very small and mainly for art and cultural students, so if you want to attend Griffith and live in Brisbane, your best bet is to register for courses at Nathan and commute (25-35 min from city center) with the cheap public transport. 

Sidenote: Griffith is opening a bigger campus in the city center for Economics and Law students by 2027 (I think)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level for a master's student in Australia in general is definitely easier than for master's students in Denmark

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is pretty low compared to KU. I do believe you can find courses with higher acamedic level if you take time to research the level of the courses beforehand.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses, I took, had no sit-in exam, which meant that the assessments were split out through the trimester. I didn't have any courses that required attendance but I know that a lot of courses do require that. Be prepared for group assignments and presentations as part of your assessment but also know, that not a single Australian attended any of my courses (solely international students) so the average Danish student is going to excel due to English proficiency

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Public transports is very very cheap. Every bus and train fare is 50p no matter the length (except if you go to the airport).

You can find excellent dining deals on EatClub meaning going out for dinner is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Griffith has an abundant of sport opportunities but as campus was far away from the city, I found myself using the social and sporting activities of other universities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Griffith has a wide range of different activities but I didn't really attend anything other than the social activities during O-week. 

The Orientation week, the sporting and cultural events of UQ and QUT are way better. I recommend attending these instead

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I think the activities during O-week is a must if you want to meet people at Griffith.

However, the sporting facilities of UQ and QUT are way better and the O-week for these Universities start 1 and 2 week after Griffith's. I really recommend going to these.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Do day trips to Gold Coast and weekend trips to Byron Bay and Noosa Heads as much as possible.

Also do a 2/3 days trip to Fraser island / K'gari

In general, Brisbane is a pretty boring city but the area around Brisbane is so beautiful and South-East Queensland is a travel hotspot with so much to do. Rent a car and explore

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are basically no local student at master's level in Australia

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. The only thing is, Australia has a lot more homeless people than Denmark. Avoid engaging with them as they do get aggressive some times and they don't like foreigners.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Being outside. Australians love being outside. They love exploring nature and socialising in the sun. Enjoy that - you will miss it when you get back to the cold.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you plan on staying in Brisbane, reach out to other international students beforehand to find accommodation. Griffith is NOT in Brisbane and the on-campus accommodation is bad and very far away.

Engage in other Universities' activities as their social and sport clubs are way better

Travel as much as possible. Brisbane is simply perfectly located for traveling

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many exchange student attend Griffith because of their Gold Coast campus. Consider registering for courses there instead of Brisbane if you enjoy surfing and going to the beach.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people you meet along the way and all the travel experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first week. It's always tough to move to the other side of the world (especially if you know no one)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
